callouts.title: 📚 Comprehensive Reference
callouts.body:
- **Generated**: 2024-12-14
- **Version**: 1.0
- **Type**: Reference Documentation

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Executive Overview** **Metadata Menu** is a powerful [[Obsidian]] [[Community Plugin]] designed for data quality enthusiasts who need systematic, typed metadata management across their vault. Unlike Obsidian's native [[Properties]] system, Metadata Menu provides comprehensive field typing, validation, autocompletion, contextual editing via multiple access points, and seamless integration with [[Dataview]] for creating editable database-style tables. The plugin bridges the gap between flexible inline [[Dataview Syntax|field notation]] (`field:: value`) and structured [[YAML Frontmatter]] properties, enabling users to transform their [[Personal Knowledge Base|PKB]] into a queryable, maintainable database with enforced data schemas.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**Navigation Guide**
This reference note is organized into 9 major sections covering installation, configuration, field architecture, fileClass systems, operational workflows, [[DataviewJS]] integration, API usage, and advanced optimization strategies. Use the table of contents below for quick navigation to specific topics, or search for technical terms using [[Wiki-Links]]. Code examples are provided throughout with actual syntax you can copy directly into your vault.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: - **Metadata-Menu**:: An Obsidian community plugin that adds typed field definitions, validation, autocompletion, and contextual editing capabilities to both YAML frontmatter properties and Dataview-style inline fields - **Field-Definition**:: A configuration specifying a field's name, type (Input, Boolean, Number, Select, Date, etc.), validation rules, and display options—enabling consistent data entry across files - **FileClass**:: A special note that acts as a metadata schema template, defining field configurations applicable to groups of files based on frontmatter attributes, tags, paths, or Dataview queries

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Central Principle** Metadata Menu transforms Obsidian from a flexible but unstructured note-taking app into a type-safe, schema-aware knowledge database while maintaining full Markdown compatibility. Every field can be edited through multiple interfaces, validated against defined constraints, and queried programmatically through Dataview—creating a best-of-both-worlds system that combines database rigor with Markdown flexibility.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**Compatibility Note**
Metadata Menu works alongside Obsidian's native Properties system (introduced in v1.4). The plugin reads and writes standard YAML frontmatter, so properties created with Metadata Menu are fully compatible with Obsidian's Properties panel and vice versa. However, Metadata Menu's advanced features (type validation, fileClass schemas, inline field support) only work when fields are defined within the plugin's settings.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**Installation Process**
Metadata Menu is installed like any [[Community Plugin]]. The setup phase focuses on configuring global settings, establishing your fileClass folder structure, and defining your first field schemas.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**Folder Exclusions**
Use the "Exclude folders from indexing" setting to prevent Metadata Menu from processing template folders, archive folders, or attachment directories. This significantly improves performance in large vaults. Use regex patterns like `^(templates|archive|attachments)/` to exclude multiple paths.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: - **Field-Type**:: The data structure and validation rules applied to a metadata field—determines what values are allowed, how they're displayed, and what editing controls are available - **Preset-Field**:: A global field definition configured in plugin settings, available in all notes regardless of fileClass assignment - **Nested-Field**:: A field that exists as a child of an Object or ObjectList parent, enabling hierarchical data structures within metadata

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Cycle Fields for Status Workflows** Use Cycle fields for linear progressions like `draft → review → final` or `todo → doing → done`. Each click advances to the next stage. Perfect for [[Kanban]]-style workflows or [[GTD]] status tracking.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Performance Impact of Auto-Update** Lookup and Formula fields with auto-update enabled can significantly slow Obsidian if you have many such fields across hundreds of notes. For large vaults (>1000 notes), prefer manual update triggered via Command Palette: `Metadata Menu: Update lookup fields`.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Nesting Limitations** While Object/ObjectList support infinite depth, Lookup, Formula, Canvas, Canvas Group, and Canvas Group Link fields CANNOT be nested. They must exist at the root level or directly under a single Object parent (not within ObjectLists).

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Field Name Uniqueness** Field names must be unique per level within a fileClass or Preset Fields. You can have a `status` field at root level AND a `status` field nested under an Object, but not two `status` fields at the same nesting level.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: - **FileClass**:: A special note stored in the designated fileClass folder that defines a metadata schema (field types, validation rules) applicable to files matching specific mapping criteria - **FileClass-Mapping**:: The process by which Metadata Menu determines which fileClass(es) apply to a given file, based on frontmatter values, tags, paths, bookmark groups, or Dataview queries - **FileClass-Inheritance**:: A mechanism allowing one fileClass to extend another, inheriting its field definitions while adding or overriding specific fields

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Mapping Priority Logic** When multiple fileClasses map to the same file, field definitions from higher-priority mappings override lower-priority ones. If `meeting` fileClass (frontmatter) and `work-note` fileClass (tag) both define a `status` field with different types, the `meeting` definition wins. Fields unique to each class are merged—the file gets ALL fields from ALL mapped classes.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**FileClass Design Patterns**
1. **Inheritance Hierarchy**: Create a base `note` fileClass with universal fields, then derive specific classes
2. **Mapping Strategy**: Use frontmatter for explicit assignment, tags for workflows, paths for organizational structures
3. **Field Granularity**: Prefer specific fileClasses with focused field sets over one mega-class with dozens of optional fields
4. **Naming Convention**: Use descriptive, hyphenated names: `project-note`, `meeting-standup`, `person-contact`

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: - **Field-Control**:: An interactive UI element that allows viewing and modifying a metadata field's value, with behavior determined by the field type - **Metadata-Menu-Button**:: A clickable icon that appears in various Obsidian interfaces (file explorer, tab headers, etc.) providing access to a note's full metadata modal - **Field-Modal**:: A popup dialog displaying all defined fields for a note, organized by fileClass, with inline editing controls

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**Disable Autocompletion Per-Field**
If autocompletion interferes with your writing flow for certain fields, you can disable it globally (Plugin Settings → toggle off) or exclude specific fields (Settings → Excluded Fields from Context Menus).

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Contextual Metadata Editing** The context menu's power lies in editing ANY note's metadata without opening it. Right-click a link in your current note → modify the linked note's fields → changes saved immediately. Essential for curating metadata across vault-wide collections.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**Per-Field Command Hotkeys**
Enable "Command Palette" in a field's definition settings to create a dedicated command for inserting that field. Assign hotkeys for frequently-used fields like `priority`, `status`, or `due-date` for keyboard-driven workflows.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Lookup and Formula Field Manual Updates** If auto-update is disabled for Lookup or Formula fields, you MUST manually trigger updates via: 1. Command Palette: `Metadata Menu: Update lookup fields` 2. Click "Update" button in Note Fields Modal 3. Right-click field → "Update lookup field" Otherwise, values remain stale even if underlying data changes.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: - **FieldModifier-API**:: A JavaScript function provided by Metadata Menu that wraps field values with interactive editing controls when embedded in DataviewJS table cells - **Editable-Dataview-Table**:: A Dataview table created with DataviewJS that uses the fieldModifier API to render field values as interactive UI controls rather than static text

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **Async/Await Requirement** The `fieldModifier` function is asynchronous, requiring: 1. `await` before each `f()` call 2. `async` in the `.map(async p => ...)` function 3. `await Promise.all()` wrapping the entire pages array Forgetting these will cause the table to render `[object Promise]` instead of controls.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: - **Metadata-Menu-API**:: A JavaScript interface exposed by the plugin at `MetadataMenu.api` or `app.plugins.plugins["metadata-menu"].api`, providing functions for reading and writing metadata programmatically

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **API Stability** The Metadata Menu API is not officially versioned or documented as stable. Method signatures may change between plugin updates. Always test API-dependent code after updating Metadata Menu.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**Scheduled Lookup Updates**
Combine with [[QuickAdd]] macros or [[Templater]] daily note templates to automatically refresh Lookup fields on a schedule. Example: Update project statistics every morning when opening daily note.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body: **ObjectList Power** ObjectList fields enable repeating substructures like multiple employees per company, multiple action items per meeting, or multiple checkpoints per project—each with their own typed fields. This transforms frontmatter into a lightweight relational database.

callouts.title: Untitled
callouts.body:
**Large Vault Re-indexing**
For vaults with 5000+ notes, re-indexing can take 30-60 seconds and temporarily freeze Obsidian. Avoid re-indexing unless absolutely necessary.

  - Official Metadata Menu documentation: https://mdelobelle.github.io/metadatamenu/

inline_fields.value: Metadata Menu treats your vault as a distributed database where each note is a record, fields are columns with schemas, and fileClasses are table definitions—enabling database-style operations while preserving Markdown flexibility.

Best practice is to create a dedicated folder outside your main content areas to store fileClass definition notes, preventing them from appearing in general searches while remaining accessible for schema management.

File-type fields support embedding dv.pages() queries that dynamically filter which files appear in the suggestion dropdown, enabling schema-enforced relationships like "only link to Person notes" or "only link to active Projects".

Object and ObjectList fields support infinite depth nesting—you can have ObjectLists containing Objects that themselves contain ObjectLists, enabling arbitrarily complex data hierarchies while maintaining full Metadata Menu editing capabilities at every level.
All notes within the specified folders (and subfolders) automatically inherit this fileClass. Supports relative paths from vault root and partial path matching.

Child fileClasses inherit ALL fields from parent classes. If a child redefines a field (same name), the child's definition overrides the parent's. The extends chain can be arbitrarily deep, enabling hierarchical schema taxonomies.

Metadata Menu's autocompletion activates when typing the field delimiter (: in frontmatter, :: for inline fields) and presents a filtered list of available fields based on current fileClass mappings plus global preset fields.

The centralized metadata management interface that displays all fields defined by a note's fileClass(es) plus global preset fields, organized into existing (with current values) and missing (available for insertion) sections, with inline editing controls for each field type.

`fieldModifier(dv, page, fieldName, options?)` where dv is the Dataview API instance, page is the current page object being processed, fieldName is the string identifier of the field to render, and options is an optional configuration object controlling display behavior.

DataviewJS tables with fieldModifier controls render more slowly than standard Dataview tables because each cell requires additional DOM manipulation. For large result sets (100+ rows), use .limit() to paginate and set alwaysOn: false to defer control rendering until user interaction.

# Meeting Note Documentation

This fileClass is used for all meeting notes. It provides structured fields for:
- Attendees tracking
- Agenda items
- Action items with assignments
- Follow-up dates

## Usage
Assign to a note by adding `fileClass: meeting` to frontmatter.

---
fileClass: meeting
---

---
fileClass: 
  - meeting
  - project-related
---

---
fileClass: work/meeting-note
---
# Maps to: 99_system/fileclasses/work/meeting-note.md

---
# In fileClass note
mapWithTag: true
tagNames: [meeting, standup, retrospective]
---

---
# In fileClass note  
path: 
  - meetings/
  - work/meetings/
  - team/standups/
---

---
# In fileClass note
bookmarkGroups: 
  - Active Projects
  - Client Work
---
Global FileClass: _base-note

# Base class: 99_system/fileclasses/note.md
---
# Fields: title, created, modified, status
---

# Derived class: 99_system/fileclasses/meeting.md

definitions.definition: Metadata Menu treats your vault as a distributed database where each note is a record, fields are columns with schemas, and fileClasses are table definitions—enabling database-style operations while preserving Markdown flexibility.

Best practice is to create a dedicated folder outside your main content areas to store fileClass definition notes, preventing them from appearing in general searches while remaining accessible for schema management.

File-type fields support embedding dv.pages() queries that dynamically filter which files appear in the suggestion dropdown, enabling schema-enforced relationships like "only link to Person notes" or "only link to active Projects".

Object and ObjectList fields support infinite depth nesting—you can have ObjectLists containing Objects that themselves contain ObjectLists, enabling arbitrarily complex data hierarchies while maintaining full Metadata Menu editing capabilities at every level.
All notes within the specified folders (and subfolders) automatically inherit this fileClass. Supports relative paths from vault root and partial path matching.

Child fileClasses inherit ALL fields from parent classes. If a child redefines a field (same name), the child's definition overrides the parent's. The extends chain can be arbitrarily deep, enabling hierarchical schema taxonomies.

Metadata Menu's autocompletion activates when typing the field delimiter (: in frontmatter, :: for inline fields) and presents a filtered list of available fields based on current fileClass mappings plus global preset fields.

The centralized metadata management interface that displays all fields defined by a note's fileClass(es) plus global preset fields, organized into existing (with current values) and missing (available for insertion) sections, with inline editing controls for each field type.

`fieldModifier(dv, page, fieldName, options?)` where dv is the Dataview API instance, page is the current page object being processed, fieldName is the string identifier of the field to render, and options is an optional configuration object controlling display behavior.

DataviewJS tables with fieldModifier controls render more slowly than standard Dataview tables because each cell requires additional DOM manipulation. For large result sets (100+ rows), use .limit() to paginate and set alwaysOn: false to defer control rendering until user interaction.
